## 2. Feature Extraction

### 2.1 FFT: hand-write it

**Recommendation: hand-write a radix-2 iterative FFT (~35 lines).** You need one forward transform of 2048 points over ~40 frames — a few milliseconds total. An npm dependency buys you nothing and costs you an install, a Vite `optimizeDeps` risk with a CommonJS module, and TS interop friction, in a 2-hour budget.

If you'd rather install: **`fft.js@4.0.4`** (Fedor Indutny, "Insanely Fast Fourier Transform (radix-4)"). I verified on the registry — it's real, pure JS, `main: lib/fft.js`, and it **ships its own `lib/fft.d.ts`** (there is no `@types/fft.js`, and you don't need one). Browser-friendly, works under Vite. API: `const f = new FFT(2048); const out = f.createComplexArray(); f.realTransform(out, input); f.completeSpectrum(out);`. Sizes must be powers of two ≥ 4. `fftjs` and `ml-fft` also exist but are less maintained.

```ts
// src/dsp/fft.ts  — precompute once, reuse across all frames
export class FFT {
  private rev: Uint32Array; private cos: Float64Array; private sin: Float64Array;
  constructor(readonly n: number) {
    const levels = Math.log2(n) | 0;
    this.rev = new Uint32Array(n);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { let x = i, r = 0; for (let j = 0; j < levels; j++) { r = (r << 1) | (x & 1); x >>= 1; } this.rev[i] = r >>> 0; }
    this.cos = new Float64Array(n >> 1); this.sin = new Float64Array(n >> 1);
    for (let i = 0; i < n >> 1; i++) { this.cos[i] = Math.cos(TWO_PI * i / n); this.sin[i] = Math.sin(TWO_PI * i / n); }
  }
  transform(re: Float64Array, im: Float64Array) {
    const { n, rev, cos, sin } = this;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const j = rev[i]; if (j > i) { let t = re[i]; re[i] = re[j]; re[j] = t; t = im[i]; im[i] = im[j]; im[j] = t; } }
    for (let size = 2; size <= n; size <<= 1) {
      const half = size >> 1, step = n / size;
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i += size) {
        for (let j = i, k = 0; j < i + half; j++, k += step) {
          const l = j + half;
          const tre =  re[l] * cos[k] + im[l] * sin[k];
          const tim = -re[l] * sin[k] + im[l] * cos[k];
          re[l] = re[j] - tre; im[l] = im[j] - tim;
          re[j] += tre;        im[j] += tim;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
export function hann(n: number): Float64Array { /* 0.5 - 0.5*cos(2πi/(n-1)) */ }
```

### 2.2 STFT parameters

| Param | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| FFT size | **2048** | 46 ms @44.1k, 21.5 Hz bins. Enough to resolve harmonics of f0 ≥ 80 Hz. |
| Hop | **512** (75% overlap) | 11.6 ms frames — fine enough to measure a 20 ms attack. |
| Window | **Hann**, normalized by `2/Σw` | Standard, good sidelobe rejection, cheap. |
| Zero-pad | none | Parabolic peak interpolation gets you sub-bin accuracy for free. |
| Sample rate | **whatever the decoded buffer has** | Never resample. Render the candidate at the same rate. |

### 2.3 f0 detection: time domain, not FFT

At 21.5 Hz bin spacing, an FFT-derived f0 for a 110 Hz sample is ±10% — useless, and every harmonic index after it is wrong. Use a **YIN-lite (normalized square difference)** on a 4096-sample window centered ~30% into the sustain region:

```ts
// src/dsp/f0.ts
export function detectF0(x: Float32Array, sr: number, offset: number)
  : { f0: number; confidence: number }
// τ ∈ [sr/2000, sr/50]  (50 Hz .. 2 kHz)
// d(τ) = Σ (x[i] - x[i+τ])²  ;  d'(τ) = d(τ) / ((1/τ) Σ_{k≤τ} d(k))   // cumulative mean normalization
// pick first τ with d'(τ) < 0.15, else global min; parabolic-interpolate τ; f0 = sr/τ
// confidence = 1 - d'(τ*)   clamped 0..1
```

Run it at 5 offsets across the sound; `f0Hz` = median, `f0DriftCents` = stdev in cents. Drift tells Claude whether the target has vibrato/glide (→ set `lfo.target='pitch'` or `master.pitchEnv`).

### 2.4 Frame anchors

Compute an RMS envelope per hop first, then pick exactly 4 anchor frames:

- `attack` = argmax(rms) — the peak frame
- `early` = peak + 20% of (endFrame − peak)
- `sustain` = peak + 55%
- `release` = peak + 85%

where `endFrame` is the last frame above −45 dB of peak. Four snapshots is the sweet spot: it captures "bright attack that dulls into a mellow sustain," which is the single most important FM-relevant shape, without a spectrogram's token cost.

### 2.5 Harmonic amplitudes

For each anchor frame, for h = 1..12:
```
bin_h = round(h * f0 * N / sr)
search bin_h ± 2 for local max, parabolic-interpolate → (peakBin, peakMag)
harmonicsDb[h] = round(20 * log10(peakMag / maxMagAcrossHarmonics)), floored at -60
partialHz[h]   = peakBin * sr / N     // kept internally for inharmonicity, not emitted
```

**Expressing harmonics in dB relative to the loudest harmonic in that frame makes them gain-invariant** — the single most important design choice here. Overall level can't leak into the spectral distance, and Claude never has to reason about absolute amplitude when it's reasoning about timbre. Frame-to-frame loudness lives separately in `rmsDb` (relative to the peak frame).

12 harmonics, not 16: at f0 = 440 Hz, harmonic 12 is 5.3 kHz, already near the top of what matters, and it saves ~50 tokens/frame.

### 2.6 The rest

```
inharmonicityCents = round( mean_{h=2..8} | 1200 * log2( partialHz[h] / (h * f0) ) | )
                     // 0 = perfectly harmonic; >30 = bell/metallic; guides non-integer ratios

noiseRatio         = 1 - (Σ energy in bins within ±2 of any h*f0) / (Σ all bin energy)
                     // 0..1 at the sustain frame; high -> feedback or high-ratio modulator

centroidRatio      = (Σ f_k |X_k| / Σ |X_k|) / f0
                     // "brightness in harmonic numbers": 1.0 = pure sine, 6.0 = very bright
                     // per-frame, so the 4 values form a brightness trajectory

oddEvenBalance     = Σ_odd energy / Σ_all harmonic energy    // sustain frame; 0.5 = balanced,
                     // >0.7 = clarinet/square (→ ratio 2:1 or 3:1), <0.35 = even-dominant
```

Amplitude envelope, from the RMS curve (post peak-normalize):
```
attackMs   = time from first frame > 1% of peak, to peak frame
sustainLevel = median(rms over the middle 40% of [peak..end]) / peak
decayMs    = time from peak to first frame within 10% of sustainLevel
releaseMs  = time from last frame > 1.3*sustainLevel to first frame < 1% of peak
durationMs = end of trimmed signal
```

### 2.7 The emitted type

// src/dsp/types.ts
export type FrameLabel = 'attack' | 'early' | 'sustain' | 'release';

export interface FrameFeature {

## 3. The Distance / Diff

The scalar exists so the UI can draw a progress bar and so you can stop iterating. The *diff* is what actually steers Claude. Design principle: **every entry says which direction to move and names an FM control that would move it.**

```ts
// src/dsp/types.ts
export type Direction = 'increase' | 'decrease';

export interface ScalarDiff {
  name: 'attackMs' | 'decayMs' | 'sustainLevel' | 'releaseMs' | 'durationMs'
      | 'f0Cents' | 'inharmonicityCents' | 'noiseRatio' | 'oddEvenBalance'
      | 'centroid.attack' | 'centroid.early' | 'centroid.sustain' | 'centroid.release'
      | 'rms.early' | 'rms.sustain' | 'rms.release';
  target: number;
  got: number;
  delta: number;        // got - target  (negative = candidate is under)
  unit: 'ms' | 'dB' | 'cents' | 'ratio' | 'x';
  direction: Direction; // which way the candidate must move
  severity: number;     // 0..1, normalized contribution to distance
  hint: string;         // FM-specific instruction
}

export interface HarmonicDiff {
  frame: FrameLabel;
  h: number;            // harmonic number 1..12
  targetDb: number;
  gotDb: number;
  deltaDb: number;      // got - target; negative = too quiet
  hint: string;
}

export interface FeatureDiff {
  distance: number;                 // 0..100, lower is better. <12 is a good match.
  breakdown: { spectrum: number; envelope: number; pitch: number; noise: number }; // each 0..100
  verdict: string;                  // one sentence
  priorities: string[];             // 3-5 ordered plain-English fixes -- read this first
  scalars: ScalarDiff[];            // only |severity| >= 0.08, sorted desc, cap 8
  harmonics: HarmonicDiff[];        // only |deltaDb| >= 5, sorted by |deltaDb| desc, cap 8
}
```

### Distance math

```
w_h        = 10^(targetDb_h / 20)                      // perceptual weight: quiet target partials matter less
spectrumD  = Σ_frames Σ_h w_h · min(|Δdb_h|, 40)/40  /  Σ_frames Σ_h w_h        // 0..1
envelopeD  = mean( min(|ΔattackMs|/150, 1), min(|ΔdecayMs|/600, 1),
                   min(|ΔsustainLevel|/0.6, 1), min(|ΔdurationMs|/800, 1) )     // 0..1
pitchD     = mean( min(|Δcents|/1200, 1), min(|ΔinharmCents|/150, 1) )          // 0..1
noiseD     = min(|ΔnoiseRatio|/0.5, 1)                                          // 0..1

distance   = 100 * (0.55*spectrumD + 0.25*envelopeD + 0.10*pitchD + 0.10*noiseD)
```

Spectrum dominates because that's what FM parameters actually control and what "sounds like the sample" means. Pitch is weighted low because you render at the target's f0 anyway — it's there only to catch a wrong-octave `ratio` on the carrier.

### Hint templates (a lookup table, ~25 lines)

```
h ≥ 6 too quiet, broadly       → "Upper harmonics are weak. Raise the modulator's level (higher
                                  modulation index) or increase feedback on op 4."
h ≥ 6 too loud, broadly        → "Too bright. Lower modulator level, or shorten the modulator's
                                  envelope decay so brightness dies away faster."
single h too quiet             → "Harmonic 3 is 12 dB too quiet. Try a modulator ratio near 3, or an
                                  op with ratio 2 feeding the carrier (ratio n produces sidebands at
                                  1±n, 1±2n...)."
odd-dominant target            → "Target is odd-harmonic dominant (0.82). Use a modulator ratio of 2
                                  against a carrier ratio of 1 — classic square/clarinet FM."
centroid falls faster in target→ "Your brightness decays too slowly. Shorten the modulator operator's
                                  env.d, or lower its env.s."
centroid rises in target       → "Target gets brighter over time — give the modulator a slow attack
                                  (env.a ≈ 200 ms)."
attackMs too slow              → "Attack is 40 ms too slow. Reduce env.a on the carrier operators."
sustainLevel too low           → "Your tone dies out; target sustains. Raise env.s on carriers."
inharmonicity target >> got    → "Target is inharmonic (48 cents). Use non-integer modulator ratios
                                  (1.41, 3.5, 7.13) or a fixedHz operator."
noiseRatio target >> got       → "Target has significant noise. Raise feedback toward 6-7, or add a
                                  high-ratio modulator (ratio 9-14) at low level."
f0 off by ~1200 cents          → "Carrier is an octave off — set the carrier operator's ratio to 1."

## 4. Offline Render-and-Analyze

### 4.1 Shared preparation (used identically on target and candidate)

```ts
// src/dsp/prepare.ts
export interface PreparedAudio { data: Float32Array; sampleRate: number; }

export function prepare(buf: AudioBuffer): PreparedAudio {
  // 1. mono-sum
  const n = buf.length, ch = buf.numberOfChannels;
  const x = new Float32Array(n);
  for (let c = 0; c < ch; c++) { const d = buf.getChannelData(c); for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) x[i] += d[i]; }
  if (ch > 1) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) x[i] /= ch;

  // 2. peak normalize FIRST (so the trim threshold is absolute)
  let peak = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) peak = Math.max(peak, Math.abs(x[i]));
  if (peak > 0) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) x[i] /= peak;

  // 3. trim: leading silence at -50 dBFS, trailing at -60 dBFS
  let s = 0; while (s < n && Math.abs(x[s]) < 0.00316) s++;
  let e = n; while (e > s && Math.abs(x[e - 1]) < 0.001) e--;

  // 4. re-normalize the trimmed region and cap at 4 s
  const out = x.slice(s, Math.min(e, s + buf.sampleRate * 4));
  let p2 = 0; for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i++) p2 = Math.max(p2, Math.abs(out[i]));
  if (p2 > 0) for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i++) out[i] /= p2;
  return { data: out, sampleRate: buf.sampleRate };
}
```

**Trimming leading silence on both signals is what makes `attackMs` comparable at all.** Without it, a target with 80 ms of pre-roll produces a bogus 80 ms attack error every iteration and Claude chases it forever.

Peak normalize (not RMS): it's deterministic, single-pass, and combined with the gain-invariant harmonic dB representation it fully removes overall level from the distance. RMS normalization would interact with `sustainLevel` in a confusing way.

### 4.2 The render

```ts
// src/audio/render.ts
import { ensureFmWorklet } from './workletLoader';
import { prepare, type PreparedAudio } from '../dsp/prepare';

export interface RenderSpec {
  f0: number;         // target's detected f0
  durationMs: number; // target's trimmed duration
  sampleRate: number; // target's sample rate -- MUST match
  gateMs: number;     // note-off point: target durationMs - releaseMs
  velocity?: number;
}

export async function renderPreset(preset: FmPreset, spec: RenderSpec): Promise<PreparedAudio> {
  const frames = Math.max(128, Math.ceil(spec.sampleRate * spec.durationMs / 1000));
  const ctx = new OfflineAudioContext(1, frames, spec.sampleRate);

  await ensureFmWorklet(ctx);          // MUST await BEFORE constructing the node

  const node = new AudioWorkletNode(ctx, 'fm-voice', {
    numberOfInputs: 0,
    numberOfOutputs: 1,
    outputChannelCount: [1],
    processorOptions: {                // synchronous + deterministic; NOT postMessage
      preset,
      f0: spec.f0,
      velocity: spec.velocity ?? 1,
      gateSamples: Math.round(spec.sampleRate * spec.gateMs / 1000),
    },
  });
  node.connect(ctx.destination);

  const buf = await ctx.startRendering();
  return prepare(buf);                 // identical path as the target
}
```

```ts
// src/audio/index.ts
export async function evaluatePreset(preset: FmPreset, target: TargetAnalysis) {
  const rendered = await renderPreset(preset, {
    f0: target.features.f0Hz,
    durationMs: target.features.durationMs,
    sampleRate: target.prepared.sampleRate,
    gateMs: Math.max(20, target.features.durationMs - target.features.amp.releaseMs),
  });
  const features = extractFeatures(rendered.data, rendered.sampleRate);
  const diff = diffFeatures(target.features, features);
  return { features, diff, rendered };
}
```

### 4.3 Gotchas — the list that will actually bite you

1. **`addModule` before node construction.** Constructing an `AudioWorkletNode` for an unregistered name throws `InvalidStateError: Unknown processor name`. The `WeakMap` cache makes the repeat calls free.
2. **`processorOptions`, not `port.postMessage`, for offline.** Port messages have no defined ordering relative to offline rendering. This is the #1 way this loop silently renders silence.
3. **Sample-rate matching.** `decodeAudioData` on an `AudioContext` **resamples to that context's rate**. So: create one live `AudioContext` at app start, decode the upload with it, and use `buffer.sampleRate` (= `ctx.sampleRate`) for every subsequent `OfflineAudioContext`. Never hardcode 44100.
4. **No priming latency** — a worklet's first `process()` writes frame 0 of the render. But do not insert a `DynamicsCompressorNode`, `ConvolverNode`, or `BiquadFilterNode` between node and destination; the first two add latency and would offset attack timing.
5. **Render quantum.** Internally the render is a whole number of 128-frame blocks, but `startRendering()` returns exactly `length` frames. Just make `length ≥ 128`.
6. **Normalize both.** Peak-normalize target and candidate via the same `prepare()`. Also `prepare()` the candidate even though it has no leading silence — running the identical code path means any bug affects both equally and cancels.
7. **Duration match.** Render exactly the target's trimmed duration so the four anchor frames land at comparable positions. If the candidate decays to silence early, `prepare()` trims it and `durationMs` becomes a real, reported error — which is correct and actionable.
8. **Run one render at a time.** Each is ~10–30 ms for a 2 s tone; serializing avoids any worklet-registration race.
9. **`return true` forever** in `process()`. Returning `false` permanently kills the node; in offline that truncates the tail.
10. Browser support: `AudioWorklet` inside `OfflineAudioContext` is Chrome 66+ / Safari 14.1+ / Firefox 76+. Target Chrome for the demo.

## 1. Stack recommendation: Vite + TS client, single Worker with `assets` binding, one Durable Object

### Workers, not Pages — and this is not a close call for you

Cloudflare's current position ([migrate-from-pages](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migration-guides/migrate-from-pages/), [convergence blog](https://blog.cloudflare.com/pages-and-workers-are-converging-into-one-experience/)): *"If you are starting a new project, use Workers instead of Pages. Pages continues to work, but new features and optimizations are focused on Workers."*

The decisive point for Claudio specifically: **a Pages Function cannot define a Durable Object class.** Cloudflare's own docs: *"to use Durable Objects with your Cloudflare Pages project, you must create a separate Worker with a Durable Object and then declare a binding to it in both your Production and Preview environments."* That is two deploys, two configs, and a cross-project binding to wire up — in a 2-hour box that's a guaranteed 20-minute tax on the highest-risk part of the build. Workers + static assets gives you frontend, API, and DO in one `wrangler deploy`.

### Durable Objects on the free plan — SQLite is required, not just preferred

From [DO pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/) and [class migrations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-objects-migrations/):

- **Workers Free plan: only SQLite-backed Durable Objects are available.** The legacy KV backend (`new_classes`) is paid-only, and only for accounts that already have a KV-backed namespace.
- So `new_sqlite_classes` is both the modern choice *and* the only thing that will deploy on free tier. Use it.
- Free limits: 100k requests/day, 13,000 GB-s/day compute, 5M storage reads/day, 100k storage writes/day, 5 GB stored. A prototype will not come close.

### `migrations` vs the new `exports` field

Cloudflare shipped a declarative `exports` field ([changelog 2026-06-30](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-06-30-declarative-do-class-exports/)) that replaces the imperative `migrations` array:

```jsonc
{ "exports": { "SessionDO": { "type": "durable-object", "storage": "sqlite" } } }
```

**Use `migrations` for this build.** Reasons: (a) `exports` is absent from the schema of the wrangler on this machine (4.70.0) so any accidental global-binary invocation hard-fails validation; (b) `exports` and `migrations` are **mutually exclusive** — a config containing both is rejected; (c) `migrations` still works unchanged and is what every example and model prior knows. Switching to `exports` is a 3-line change in a later session.

### Vite plugin, not two dev servers

`@cloudflare/vite-plugin` runs your Worker + DO in the real workerd runtime inside `vite dev`. One command, one process, HMR on the client, real DO semantics locally. Confirmed setup from [vite-plugin/get-started](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/get-started/) — note their example uses `compatibility_date: "2026-08-14"`, i.e. current as of today.

```

Every key here is confirmed present in the installed `config-schema.json`. The `assets` object accepts exactly `directory`, `binding`, `html_handling`, `not_found_handling` (`single-page-application` | `404-page` | `none`), `run_worker_first` (string[] or boolean) — `additionalProperties: false`, so a typo fails validation rather than being silently ignored.

If routing misbehaves, the fallback is to drop `run_worker_first` entirely and have the Worker do `if (!url.pathname.startsWith("/api/")) return env.ASSETS.fetch(request)` — keep that line in the code regardless as a safety net.

## 4. Session state design (the Durable Object)

**One DO instance per session**, addressed by a client-generated UUID: `env.SESSION.getByName(sessionId)`. This is the correct coordination atom — a session owns exactly one Claude conversation and one render loop, and nothing crosses sessions. Do **not** create a global DO.

### Storage: SQLite, two tables

```ts
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(id = 1), json TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, json TEXT NOT NULL);
```

Rationale for two tables rather than one `ctx.storage.put("state", ...)` blob: the Anthropic `MessageParam[]` grows unboundedly across chat turns and would eventually exceed the 128 KiB KV value limit. One row per message dodges that entirely, costs ~8 lines, and gives you a natural `SELECT json FROM messages ORDER BY seq` reload. Schema creation goes in the constructor under `ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile()` — and nowhere else (never hold `blockConcurrencyWhile` across the Claude fetch).

### What's stored

```ts
// src/shared/protocol.ts
export type SessionStatus = "idle" | "thinking" | "awaiting_render" | "done" | "error";

export interface SessionMeta {
  status: SessionStatus;
  target: FeatureVector | null;
  targetInfo: { filename: string; durationSec: number; sampleRate: number } | null;
  iteration: number;             // completed render+analyze cycles
  maxIterations: number;         // 3
  pendingToolUseId: string | null;   // ← the paused tool_use, the crux of the whole design
  pendingPresetId: string | null;    // ← idempotency / stale-render guard
  history: Attempt[];
  bestPresetId: string | null;
  createdAt: number;
}

export interface Attempt {
  presetId: string;
  preset: Preset;
  rationale: string;
  features: FeatureVector | null;   // null until the browser reports back
  distance: number | null;
}
```

`meta` is persisted as a single JSON row after every mutation (persist-then-cache). `messages` is append-only. The in-memory copy is hydrated once in the constructor.

### RPC surface (not `fetch()`)

Compatibility date is 2026-08-14, well past the ≥ 2024-04-03 requirement for RPC, so use typed RPC methods — they're less code than a nested fetch router and the types flow end-to-end:

```ts
export class SessionDO extends DurableObject<Env> {
  async setTarget(target: FeatureVector, info: TargetInfo): Promise<Step>;
  async submitAnalysis(presetId: string, features: FeatureVector, diff: FeatureDiff): Promise<Step>;
  async submitRenderError(presetId: string, message: string): Promise<Step>;
  async chat(message: string): Promise<Step>;
  async snapshot(): Promise<SessionSnapshot>;
}
```

Arguments and returns are plain JSON objects — structured-cloneable, so RPC is happy.

## 5. The agent loop protocol — the centerpiece

### The problem restated

The render+analyze half of the loop lives in the browser (Web Audio). The Claude conversation lives in the DO. Claude's turn *pauses* at a `tool_use` block and can only be resumed by appending a matching `tool_result` — but the data for that `tool_result` won't exist until an HTTP round trip later. So the paused conversation must survive between requests.

### The solution: persist the `tool_use_id`, drive everything through one `Step` union

The DO stores `pendingToolUseId` alongside the message log. When the browser reports back, the DO synthesizes the `tool_result` with that exact id, appends it, and calls Claude again. The conversation never knows there was a gap.

```ts
// src/shared/protocol.ts
export type Step =
  | { kind: "render";  presetId: string; preset: Preset; rationale: string;
      iteration: number; iterationsRemaining: number; note: string }
  | { kind: "message"; text: string; preset: Preset | null; iteration: number }
  | { kind: "done";    text: string; preset: Preset; presetId: string; distance: number | null }
  | { kind: "error";   message: string; retryable: boolean };
```

**Every endpoint returns a `Step`.** That unification is what keeps this small — and it means a chat turn ("brighter") flows through the *identical* client code path as the initial refinement loop, because Claude answering "brighter" by calling `propose_preset` just yields another `{kind:"render"}`.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/session` | — | `{ sessionId: string }` |
| `POST` | `/api/session/:id/target` | `{ features: FeatureVector, info: TargetInfo }` | `Step` |
| `POST` | `/api/session/:id/analysis` | `{ presetId, features: FeatureVector, diff: FeatureDiff }` | `Step` |
| `POST` | `/api/session/:id/render-error` | `{ presetId, message: string }` | `Step` |
| `POST` | `/api/session/:id/chat` | `{ message: string }` | `Step` |
| `GET` | `/api/session/:id` | — | `SessionSnapshot` |

### The client is ~10 lines

```ts
// src/client/main.ts
async function drain(step: Step) {
  while (step.kind === "render") {
    ui.showAttempt(step);
    try {
      const buf   = await renderPreset(step.preset);        // OfflineAudioContext
      const got   = analyze(buf);                            // same STFT features as target
      const diff  = compareFeatures(targetFeatures, got);
      step = await api.submitAnalysis(sessionId, step.presetId, got, diff);
    } catch (e) {
      // a bad preset must not wedge the loop — tell the agent, let it retry
      step = await api.submitRenderError(sessionId, step.presetId, String(e));
    }
  }
  ui.showFinal(step);
}
```

The `try/catch → submitRenderError` path is **mandatory, not optional polish**. Structured-output JSON Schema cannot express numeric ranges (see §6), so Claude *can* hand you `ratio: 240` or `env.a: -1`. Without the catch, one bad preset stalls the session forever. With it, the DO appends a `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and Claude self-corrects — which is arguably a better demo than silent clamping.

### The DO driver

```ts
private async runClaude(force: boolean): Promise<Step> {
  this.meta.status = "thinking"; this.persist();
  try {
    const res = await this.anthropic.messages.create({
      model: "claude-sonnet-5",
      max_tokens: 2048,
      thinking: { type: "adaptive" },
      output_config: { effort: "low" },
      system: SYSTEM_BLOCKS,              // cache_control on last block
      tools: TOOLS,
      tool_choice: force
        ? { type: "any",  disable_parallel_tool_use: true }   // refinement loop: must act
        : { type: "auto", disable_parallel_tool_use: true },  // chat: may just answer
      messages: this.loadMessages(),
    });

    this.appendMessage({ role: "assistant", content: res.content });

    const text = res.content.filter(b => b.type === "text").map(b => b.text).join("");
    const tool = res.content.find(b => b.type === "tool_use");

    if (!tool) { this.meta.status = "idle"; this.persist(); return { kind: "message", text, ... }; }

    if (tool.name === "propose_preset") {
      const presetId = crypto.randomUUID();
      this.meta.pendingToolUseId = tool.id;       // ← the paused state, persisted
      this.meta.pendingPresetId  = presetId;
      this.meta.status = "awaiting_render";
      this.meta.history.push({ presetId, preset: tool.input.preset, rationale: tool.input.rationale,
                               features: null, distance: null });
      this.persist();
      return { kind: "render", presetId, preset: tool.input.preset,
               rationale: tool.input.rationale, note: text,
               iteration: this.meta.iteration,
               iterationsRemaining: this.meta.maxIterations - this.meta.iteration };
    }

    if (tool.name === "finalize") {
      this.appendMessage({ role: "user", content: [
        { type: "tool_result", tool_use_id: tool.id, content: "Finalized." }] });
      this.meta.status = "done"; this.meta.pendingToolUseId = null; this.persist();
      return { kind: "done", text, preset: tool.input.preset, ... };
    }
  } catch (e) {
    // CRITICAL: never leave status stuck on "thinking" — that wedges the session
    this.meta.status = this.meta.pendingToolUseId ? "awaiting_render" : "idle";
    this.persist();
    return { kind: "error", message: String(e), retryable: true };
  }
}
```

And the resume:

```ts
async submitAnalysis(presetId: string, features: FeatureVector, diff: FeatureDiff): Promise<Step> {
  if (this.meta.status !== "awaiting_render") throw new Error("not awaiting a render");
  if (presetId !== this.meta.pendingPresetId) throw new Error("stale render");   // idempotency guard

  this.meta.iteration += 1;
  const remaining = this.meta.maxIterations - this.meta.iteration;

  this.appendMessage({ role: "user", content: [{
    type: "tool_result",
    tool_use_id: this.meta.pendingToolUseId!,        // ← the id we parked one HTTP request ago
    content: JSON.stringify({
      distance: diff.distance,
      per_feature: diff.perFeature,   // { centroidHz: {target, got, delta_pct}, ... }
      iteration: this.meta.iteration,
      iterations_remaining: remaining,
      best_distance_so_far: this.bestDistance(),
      note: remaining === 0
        ? "Budget exhausted. Call finalize now with the best preset you have found."
        : "Propose your next preset, or call finalize if this is close enough."
    }),
  }]});
  this.meta.pendingToolUseId = null;
  this.recordResult(presetId, features, diff.distance);
  this.persist();

  return this.runClaude(/* force */ true);
}
```

The `presetId` equality check is the whole idempotency story: a double-click, a retry, or a reload mid-render can't desync the conversation — the second POST just 409s.

### WebSockets vs plain HTTP — recommendation: **plain HTTP**

Take HTTP request/response. Justification for a 2-hour box:

**For HTTP:**
- The protocol is *inherently* request/response. There is exactly one outstanding operation at any moment, and nothing ever happens server-side without the client asking. There is no server-push requirement — the primary motivation for WebSockets simply isn't present.
- With DO RPC, the entire transport is `const step = await env.SESSION.getByName(id).submitAnalysis(...)`. That's the whole thing.
- Reload/reconnect is free: `GET /api/session/:id` returns the snapshot and the client resumes from `status`.

**Against WebSockets here:**
- The hibernation API needs `acceptWebSocket`, `webSocketMessage`, `webSocketClose`, plus your own message framing, request/response correlation ids, and client-side reconnect. Realistically 40–50 minutes — a quarter of the budget — and it's the layer most likely to differ between `vite dev` and production.
- It buys you exactly one thing you'd notice: token streaming in chat. A spinner is acceptable in a prototype.
- Non-streaming also gives you a single code path for extracting `tool_use` (no `content_block_delta` accumulation, no partial-JSON assembly).

**The latency check that makes this safe:** Cloudflare's HTTP request ceiling is ~100s. A non-streaming `claude-sonnet-5` call at `effort: "low"` with `max_tokens: 2048` lands in roughly 3–10s. Comfortable margin. If you later find chat feels sluggish, add SSE (`ReadableStream` from the Worker) before reaching for WebSockets — SSE is one-directional and half the work.

## 6. Claude API usage

### Model: `claude-sonnet-5`

You asked for a fast model for the refine iterations, and this is the right pick over Haiku. Sonnet 5 delivers near-Opus quality on agentic/tool-use work at $3/$15 per MTok (**$2/$10 introductory through 2026-08-31 — you're inside that window today**), with a 1M context window. Haiku 4.5 would be cheaper but the sound-design reasoning — mapping a spectral-centroid delta to a modulation-index change — is exactly the kind of causal inference where the tier gap shows.

Request parameters:

```ts
{
  model: "claude-sonnet-5",
  max_tokens: 2048,                          // preset JSON + one rationale sentence is small
  thinking: { type: "adaptive" },            // NOT "disabled" — see below
  output_config: { effort: "low" },          // the speed lever
  tool_choice: { type: "any", disable_parallel_tool_use: true },
}
```

Three non-obvious points:

1. **Do not set `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`.** On Sonnet 5, thinking-off makes the model *less* likely to reach for tools — which is precisely the behavior your loop depends on. Use `thinking: {type:"adaptive"}` and control speed with `effort: "low"` instead. On Sonnet 5 adaptive is the default anyway (omitting `thinking` runs adaptive — a change from Sonnet 4.6).
2. **`disable_parallel_tool_use: true` is load-bearing.** Without it, Claude may emit two `propose_preset` blocks in one turn, and you can only render one at a time. You'd have to either render both or return a malformed result set. Force one.
3. **`tool_choice: {type:"any"}` during refinement, `{type:"auto"}` during chat.** In the loop you want action, not commentary. In chat, "what does the feedback parameter do?" should get a text answer, not a forced preset.

### Tool definitions

```ts
const OPERATOR_SCHEMA = {
  type: "object",
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ["ratio", "fixedHz", "level", "detune", "env", "velSens"],
  properties: {
    ratio:   { type: "number", description: "Frequency multiple of the played note. 0.25–16. Integer ratios (1,2,3,4) give harmonic tones; non-integer (1.41, 3.14, 7.13) give bell/metallic inharmonicity." },
    fixedHz: { type: "number", description: "If greater than 0, this operator runs at a fixed absolute frequency in Hz and ignores `ratio`. Use 0 for normal ratio mode. Useful for fixed formants or noise-like beds." },
    level:   { type: "number", description: "0–1. For a carrier this is output amplitude; for a modulator this is the modulation index — the single most powerful control over brightness/harmonic count." },
    detune:  { type: "number", description: "Cents, -100 to 100. Small values thicken; large values on a modulator add inharmonicity and beating." },
    env: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["a", "d", "s", "r"],
      properties: {
        a: { type: "number", description: "Attack seconds, 0.001–2." },
        d: { type: "number", description: "Decay seconds, 0.001–4." },
        s: { type: "number", description: "Sustain level 0–1." },
        r: { type: "number", description: "Release seconds, 0.001–4." }
      }
    },
    velSens: { type: "number", description: "0–1 velocity sensitivity." }
  }
} as const;

const PRESET_SCHEMA = {
  type: "object",
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ["algorithm", "feedback", "ops", "lfo", "master"],
  properties: {
    algorithm: { type: "integer", description: "0–7. See the algorithm table in the system prompt." },
    feedback:  { type: "number", description: "0–1. Self-modulation of the feedback operator. Above ~0.7 it approaches noise — the main lever for gritty/noisy timbres." },
    ops: { type: "array", items: OPERATOR_SCHEMA, description: "Exactly 4 operators, index 0–3. Which are carriers vs modulators is determined by `algorithm`." },
    lfo: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["rate", "depth", "target"],
      properties: {
        rate:   { type: "number", description: "Hz, 0.05–20." },
        depth:  { type: "number", description: "0–1." },
        target: { type: "string", enum: ["pitch", "amp", "mod"] }
      }
    },
    master: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["gain", "pitchEnv"],
      properties: {
        gain:     { type: "number", description: "0–1 output gain." },
        pitchEnv: { type: "number", description: "-1 to 1. Short pitch sweep at note start; positive values give percussive attack 'blip'." }
      }
    }
  }
} as const;

export const TOOLS = [
  {
    name: "propose_preset",
    strict: true,
    description:
      "Propose a 4-operator FM preset to test. The browser will render this preset offline with " +
      "OfflineAudioContext, compute the exact same STFT feature vector that was computed for the " +
      "target sample, and return you a per-feature diff plus a scalar distance as the tool result. " +
      "This is your measurement instrument — use it to test one hypothesis at a time. " +
      "You must call this at least once before calling finalize.",
    input_schema: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["preset", "rationale"],
      properties: {
        preset: PRESET_SCHEMA,
        rationale: { type: "string", description: "One sentence: what you changed relative to the previous attempt, and which specific feature you expect it to move and in which direction." }
      }
    }
  },
  {
    name: "finalize",
    strict: true,
    description:
      "Lock in your best preset and stop iterating. Call this when the distance has stopped " +
      "improving, the match is subjectively good enough, or `iterations_remaining` has reached 0.",
    input_schema: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["preset", "rationale"],
      properties: {
        preset: PRESET_SCHEMA,
        rationale: { type: "string", description: "Two or three sentences for the user: what kind of sound this is, which FM techniques produce it, and where it still differs from the target." }
      }
    }
  }
];
```

**Two schema gotchas that will bite you if unflagged:**

1. **`strict: true` requires every property in `required` and `additionalProperties: false` everywhere.** That kills an optional `fixedHz?`. Two fixes: the `0` sentinel used above (simplest — one line in the engine: `const f = op.fixedHz > 0 ? op.fixedHz : noteHz * op.ratio`), or `{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"},{"type":"null"}]}` with `fixedHz` still listed in `required`. **Take the sentinel.** Make sure the DSP agent knows about it — it belongs in `src/shared/preset.ts` as a documented comment.
2. **Structured outputs do not support `minimum` / `maximum` / `minLength` / array-length constraints.** You cannot enforce "ratio between 0.25 and 16" or "exactly 4 operators" in the schema. Ranges live in the `description` strings (as above), and enforcement is the client-side `try/catch → submitRenderError` path plus, if there's time, a `sanitizePreset()` clamp.

### System prompt sketch

Five sections. The critical structural rule: **section 2 is generated from `src/shared/algorithms.ts`, never hand-written**, so the prompt cannot drift from the engine.

```ts
// src/worker/agent.ts
export const SYSTEM_BLOCKS = [
  { type: "text", text: `
You are a sound designer operating a 4-operator FM synthesizer through a closed measurement loop.

## How this loop works
The user uploaded an audio sample. The browser computed an STFT-derived feature vector from it —
that is your TARGET. You propose a preset with the propose_preset tool. The browser renders it
offline, computes the identical feature vector, and returns you a per-feature diff. You then
propose a refinement. You have a small, fixed iteration budget; every tool result tells you how
many iterations remain.

You are matching a *feature vector*, not a waveform. Your goal is to reduce the reported distance
while producing a preset that is musically sensible. Change one or two things per iteration and
say what you expect them to do — a controlled experiment beats a shotgun.

## The 4-operator FM engine
Four operators. Each is a sine oscillator with its own frequency ratio (or fixed Hz), output
level, detune, and ADSR envelope. Whether an operator is a CARRIER (its output is heard) or a
MODULATOR (its output modulates another operator's phase) is determined entirely by the algorithm.

Core causal facts, in rough order of leverage:
- A modulator's \`level\` is the modulation index. Raising it adds sidebands: more partials,
  brighter, denser. This is your primary brightness control.
- A modulator's \`ratio\` sets sideband SPACING. Integer ratios (1,2,3,4) produce harmonic,
  pitched, instrument-like spectra. Non-integer ratios (1.41, 2.73, 3.14, 7.13) produce
  inharmonic, bell-like, metallic, or clangorous spectra.
- Ratio 1:1 gives a sawtooth-ish full harmonic series. 2:1 emphasises even harmonics
  (clarinet/hollow character comes from odd-only, which you get around 3:1 with low index).
- \`feedback\` is an operator modulating itself. Low values add harmonics smoothly;
  above roughly 0.7 the spectrum breaks into noise. This is how you get grit, breath, and
  noise beds without a noise generator.
- The MODULATOR's envelope shapes TIMBRE OVER TIME; the CARRIER's envelope shapes LOUDNESS
  over time. A modulator decay shorter than the carrier decay gives the classic
  "bright attack that mellows out" — the signature of struck and plucked sounds.
- \`master.pitchEnv\` is a fast pitch sweep at note start. Positive values give a percussive
  click/blip attack (drums, mallets).
- \`detune\` on modulators adds beating and mild inharmonicity; on carriers it thickens.

## The 8 algorithms
${renderAlgorithmTable(ALGORITHMS)}   // generated from src/shared/algorithms.ts

## How to read the feature diff
Each tool result gives you \`distance\` (lower is better) and \`per_feature\`, where each entry is
{ target, got, delta_pct }. Positive delta_pct means your render measured HIGHER than the target.

- centroidHz        Spectral brightness. Too low -> raise modulator level, or raise modulator
                    ratio. Too high -> lower modulator level first; it is the blunter instrument.
- centroidSlope     How brightness changes from attack to decay. Target more negative than yours
                    -> shorten the modulator's env.d relative to the carrier's.
- flatness          0 = pure tone, 1 = noise. Too low -> raise feedback, or move a modulator to a
                    non-integer ratio. Too high -> reduce feedback and return to integer ratios.
- inharmonicity     Directly controlled by non-integer modulator ratios and heavy detune.
- oddEvenRatio      Ratio choice. ~3:1 with modest index leans odd (hollow, clarinet-like);
                    ~2:1 gives a fuller odd+even spectrum.
- attackMs          Carrier env.a. For attack *bite* specifically, shorten the modulator's env.a
                    while keeping its level high.
- decayMs / sustainLevel / releaseMs   Carrier env.d / env.s / env.r.
- bands[]           Coarse log-spaced spectral shape. A target with energy concentrated in a
                    single band region suggests a simpler algorithm with fewer parallel carriers;
                    energy spread across many bands suggests parallel carriers or higher feedback.

## Working rules
1. First proposal: read the target vector holistically and pick a plausible ARCHETYPE
   (struck metal / plucked string / brass / electric piano / bass / pad / noisy percussion),
   then instantiate it. Do not start from a default sine.
2. Each later proposal: pick the ONE or TWO features with the largest weighted error and address
   them specifically. State the expectation in \`rationale\`.
3. If a change moved a feature the wrong way, reverse it rather than compounding it.
4. When \`iterations_remaining\` reaches 0, call finalize with the best preset you have seen,
   not necessarily the most recent one.
5. Later, the user will chat with you to tweak the sound in plain language ("brighter",
   "more attack bite", "less metallic"). Translate those to specific parameter moves using the
   causal facts above, propose the preset, and let the measurement confirm it.
`.trim(),
    cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }   // system + tools are stable; cache them
  }
];
```

`cache_control` on the last system block caches tools + system together (render order is tools → system → messages). Sonnet 5's minimum cacheable prefix is 1024 tokens; the block above plus the tool schemas clears that comfortably. Every turn after the first in a session reads it at ~0.1×. Verify with `response.usage.cache_read_input_tokens` — if it's 0 across turns, something in the prefix is varying.

| **1** | 0:00–0:15 | `npm init`, install deps, `vite.config.ts`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `index.html`, Worker returning `{ok:true}` on `/api/ping`. `wrangler secret put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. `wrangler types`. **`npm run deploy`.** | A live `*.workers.dev` URL serving the page and answering `/api/ping` |
| **2** | 0:15–0:30 | Write `src/shared/{preset,algorithms,features,protocol}.ts`. **Hand to the DSP agent and freeze.** | Both agents compile against the same types |
| **3** | 0:30–0:45 | `SessionDO`: SQLite init, `SessionMeta`, all RPC methods, Worker `/api/*` router. `runClaude()` returns a **hardcoded** preset and cycles the state machine. Deploy. | `curl` the target endpoint → get a `{kind:"render"}` |

### Synth engine: use an existing library

**Do not hand-write the FM engine.** FM is solved; the prototype's value is in the upload→preset path and the agent-driven exploration loop, not in DSP craftsmanship. The engine is a means to an end and should consume as little of the 2 hours as possible. Library survey in progress (Tone.js is the leading candidate — it has offline rendering via `Tone.Offline()`, which the compare step needs). If the chosen library can't do 4 operators with 8 algorithms, we trim the preset schema to fit the library rather than writing DSP to fit the schema.

---

## Audio analysis layer

This is where the DSP effort actually goes. Three functions are the whole contract between the audio layer and the agent layer:

```ts
// src/audio/index.ts
analyzeTarget(file: File): Promise<TargetAnalysis>          // features -> Claude, audio stays local
evaluatePreset(preset, target): Promise<{ features, diff, buffer }>   // diff -> Claude
playNote(preset, midi, velocity): () => void                // live audition
```

### Feature summary (what Claude reads on turn 1)

A compact, gain-invariant, musician-legible JSON (~300–350 tokens). Not a spectrogram.

- `f0Hz`, `f0Confidence`, `f0DriftCents` — pitch, plus whether it's even pitched, plus vibrato/glide.
- `amp: { attackMs, decayMs, sustainLevel, releaseMs }`, `durationMs`.
- `inharmonicityCents` — 0 = harmonic, >30 = bell/metallic. Drives non-integer ratios.
- `noiseRatio`, `oddEvenBalance` — drives feedback and ratio choice.
- `frames[4]` — snapshots at **attack / early / sustain / release**, each with `rmsDb`, `centroidRatio` (brightness expressed in harmonic numbers), and `harmonicsDb[12]`.

**Key design choice: harmonic amplitudes are in dB relative to the loudest harmonic *in that frame*.** That makes them gain-invariant, so overall level can never leak into the spectral distance and Claude never reasons about absolute amplitude when it's reasoning about timbre. Four time anchors (not one, not a full spectrogram) is what captures "bright attack that dulls into a mellow sustain" — the single most FM-relevant shape — at negligible token cost.

STFT params: 2048-point FFT, 512 hop (75% overlap), Hann window, no resampling. f0 comes from a time-domain NSDF/YIN-lite estimator, **not** from FFT bins — at 21.5 Hz bin spacing an FFT f0 for a low sample is off by ~10%, which corrupts every harmonic index downstream.

### The diff (what actually steers the agent)

The scalar distance exists for the progress bar and the stop condition. The **diff** is what makes the loop converge, and its design rule is: *every entry names a direction to move and an FM control that would move it.*

```ts
FeatureDiff = {
  distance: number            // 0..100, <12 is a good match
  breakdown: { spectrum, envelope, pitch, noise }
  verdict: string             // one sentence
  priorities: string[]        // 3-5 ordered plain-English fixes — the agent reads this first
  scalars: ScalarDiff[]       // {name, target, got, delta, unit, direction, severity, hint}
  harmonics: HarmonicDiff[]   // {frame, h, targetDb, gotDb, deltaDb, hint}
}
```

`distance = 100 * (0.55*spectrum + 0.25*envelope + 0.10*pitch + 0.10*noise)`. Spectrum dominates because that is what FM parameters control and what "sounds like the sample" means. Pitch is weighted low because we render at the target's detected f0 anyway — it's only there to catch a wrong-octave carrier.

Hints come from a ~25-line lookup table translating numeric deltas into FM instructions, e.g. *"Harmonic 7 is 32 dB too quiet at the attack — raise the modulator's peak level"*, *"Target's brightness collapses within 300 ms; yours barely changes — shorten the modulator's decay"*, *"Target is inharmonic (41 cents) — use a non-integer modulator ratio."* A populated diff runs ~450 tokens and an FM programmer could act on it directly.

### Render-and-analyze path

Target and candidate go through **the identical** `prepare()`: mono-sum → peak-normalize → trim leading silence (−50 dBFS) and trailing (−60 dBFS) → re-normalize → cap at 4 s.

Trimming both is load-bearing: without it a target with 80 ms of pre-roll reports a phantom 80 ms attack error on every iteration and the agent chases it forever. Running the candidate through the same code path means any extractor bug affects both signals equally and cancels.

Render the candidate at the target's detected f0, for the target's trimmed duration, **at the target's sample rate**. Gotcha: `decodeAudioData` resamples to the decoding context's rate — create one live `AudioContext` at startup, decode the upload with it, and use `buffer.sampleRate` everywhere after. Never hardcode 44100.

---

# Claudio — Agent-Loop FM Sound Design Tool

## Context

`/Users/willstockwell/agent-workspace/claudio/develop` is an empty repo (one README, one commit, branch `develop`). We are building a **2-hour timeboxed prototype** of a browser-based FM synthesizer driven by a Claude agent loop.

The product idea: a user uploads an audio sample. The browser analyzes it via STFT into a compact feature summary. A Claude agent proposes a 4-operator FM preset. The browser renders that preset offline, extracts the *same* features, and reports a distance + per-feature diff back to the agent, which refines. After 2–3 iterations the user can keep tweaking the preset conversationally ("brighter", "more attack bite").

The interesting claim being tested is the **closed render-compare loop** — the agent isn't guessing once, it's getting numeric feedback on its own output and correcting. That is the part worth protecting inside the timebox.

### Decisions already made (by the user)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Synth | 4 operators, ~8 fixed algorithms |
| Agent loop | Closed loop with render-compare, 2–3 iterations |
| Deployment | Deployed to Cloudflare (Pages/Worker + Durable Object session) |
| Input | File upload (drag/drop); baked-in starter samples are a later nice-to-have |
| LLM | Anthropic API, user has a key ready |

### Environment findings

- Node v25.8.0, npm 11.19.0, `npx wrangler` 4.123.0 available.
- **Not authenticated to Cloudflare** — no `~/.wrangler` config dir. The user will need to run `! npx wrangler login` (interactive) before the deploy step.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is not in the shell env. It goes in as a Worker secret (`wrangler secret put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), never in the client bundle.

This document ships **in the repo** as `PLAN.md`, not just in the plan scratch dir. # Claudio — 2-Hour Prototype Plan (scaffold, session state, agent protocol, build order)

## 0. Environment facts I verified

| Fact | Value | How verified |
|---|---|---|
| Repo | `/Users/willstockwell/agent-workspace/claudio/develop`, branch `develop`, one commit (`README.md`), `main` exists | `git log`, `ls` |
| Node / npm | v25.8.0 / 11.19.0 | `node -v` |
| Global wrangler | **4.70.0** at `/usr/local/bin/wrangler` — its `config-schema.json` has **no `exports` key** | inspected `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json` |
| `npx wrangler` | 4.123.0 (downloads latest) | `npx wrangler --version` |

**Consequence:** pin `wrangler` in `devDependencies` and always invoke via `npx wrangler` / npm scripts, so dev and deploy use the same binary. Never call the global one.

---

## 1. Stack recommendation: Vite + TS client, single Worker with `assets` binding, one Durable Object

### Workers, not Pages — and this is not a close call for you

Cloudflare's current position ([migrate-from-pages](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migration-guides/migrate-from-pages/), [convergence blog](https://blog.cloudflare.com/pages-and-workers-are-converging-into-one-experience/)): *"If you are starting a new project, use Workers instead of Pages. Pages continues to work, but new features and optimizations are focused on Workers."*

The decisive point for Claudio specifically: **a Pages Function cannot define a Durable Object class.** Cloudflare's own docs: *"to use Durable Objects with your Cloudflare Pages project, you must create a separate Worker with a Durable Object and then declare a binding to it in both your Production and Preview environments."* That is two deploys, two configs, and a cross-project binding to wire up — in a 2-hour box that's a guaranteed 20-minute tax on the highest-risk part of the build. Workers + static assets gives you frontend, API, and DO in one `wrangler deploy`.

### Durable Objects on the free plan — SQLite is required, not just preferred

From [DO pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/) and [class migrations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-objects-migrations/):

- **Workers Free plan: only SQLite-backed Durable Objects are available.** The legacy KV backend (`new_classes`) is paid-only, and only for accounts that already have a KV-backed namespace.
- So `new_sqlite_classes` is both the modern choice *and* the only thing that will deploy on free tier. Use it.
- Free limits: 100k requests/day, 13,000 GB-s/day compute, 5M storage reads/day, 100k storage writes/day, 5 GB stored. A prototype will not come close.

### `migrations` vs the new `exports` field

Cloudflare shipped a declarative `exports` field ([changelog 2026-06-30](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-06-30-declarative-do-class-exports/)) that replaces the imperative `migrations` array:

```jsonc
{ "exports": { "SessionDO": { "type": "durable-object", "storage": "sqlite" } } }
```

**Use `migrations` for this build.** Reasons: (a) `exports` is absent from the schema of the wrangler on this machine (4.70.0) so any accidental global-binary invocation hard-fails validation; (b) `exports` and `migrations` are **mutually exclusive** — a config containing both is rejected; (c) `migrations` still works unchanged and is what every example and model prior knows. Switching to `exports` is a 3-line change in a later session.

### Vite plugin, not two dev servers

`@cloudflare/vite-plugin` runs your Worker + DO in the real workerd runtime inside `vite dev`. One command, one process, HMR on the client, real DO semantics locally. Confirmed setup from [vite-plugin/get-started](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/get-started/) — note their example uses `compatibility_date: "2026-08-14"`, i.e. current as of today.

---

## 2. Repo layout

```

├── package.json

## 4. Session state design (the Durable Object)

**One DO instance per session**, addressed by a client-generated UUID: `env.SESSION.getByName(sessionId)`. This is the correct coordination atom — a session owns exactly one Claude conversation and one render loop, and nothing crosses sessions. Do **not** create a global DO.

### Storage: SQLite, two tables

```ts
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(id = 1), json TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, json TEXT NOT NULL);
```

Rationale for two tables rather than one `ctx.storage.put("state", ...)` blob: the Anthropic `MessageParam[]` grows unboundedly across chat turns and would eventually exceed the 128 KiB KV value limit. One row per message dodges that entirely, costs ~8 lines, and gives you a natural `SELECT json FROM messages ORDER BY seq` reload. Schema creation goes in the constructor under `ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile()` — and nowhere else (never hold `blockConcurrencyWhile` across the Claude fetch).

### What's stored

```ts
// src/shared/protocol.ts
export type SessionStatus = "idle" | "thinking" | "awaiting_render" | "done" | "error";

export interface SessionMeta {
  status: SessionStatus;
  target: FeatureVector | null;
  targetInfo: { filename: string; durationSec: number; sampleRate: number } | null;
  iteration: number;             // completed render+analyze cycles
  maxIterations: number;         // 3
  pendingToolUseId: string | null;   // ← the paused tool_use, the crux of the whole design
  pendingPresetId: string | null;    // ← idempotency / stale-render guard
  history: Attempt[];
  bestPresetId: string | null;
  createdAt: number;
}

export interface Attempt {
  presetId: string;
  preset: Preset;
  rationale: string;
  features: FeatureVector | null;   // null until the browser reports back
  distance: number | null;
}
```

`meta` is persisted as a single JSON row after every mutation (persist-then-cache). `messages` is append-only. The in-memory copy is hydrated once in the constructor.

### RPC surface (not `fetch()`)

Compatibility date is 2026-08-14, well past the ≥ 2024-04-03 requirement for RPC, so use typed RPC methods — they're less code than a nested fetch router and the types flow end-to-end:

```ts
export class SessionDO extends DurableObject<Env> {
  async setTarget(target: FeatureVector, info: TargetInfo): Promise<Step>;
  async submitAnalysis(presetId: string, features: FeatureVector, diff: FeatureDiff): Promise<Step>;
  async submitRenderError(presetId: string, message: string): Promise<Step>;
  async chat(message: string): Promise<Step>;
  async snapshot(): Promise<SessionSnapshot>;
}
```

Arguments and returns are plain JSON objects — structured-cloneable, so RPC is happy.

## 5. The agent loop protocol — the centerpiece

### The problem restated

The render+analyze half of the loop lives in the browser (Web Audio). The Claude conversation lives in the DO. Claude's turn *pauses* at a `tool_use` block and can only be resumed by appending a matching `tool_result` — but the data for that `tool_result` won't exist until an HTTP round trip later. So the paused conversation must survive between requests.

### The solution: persist the `tool_use_id`, drive everything through one `Step` union

The DO stores `pendingToolUseId` alongside the message log. When the browser reports back, the DO synthesizes the `tool_result` with that exact id, appends it, and calls Claude again. The conversation never knows there was a gap.

```ts
// src/shared/protocol.ts
export type Step =
  | { kind: "render";  presetId: string; preset: Preset; rationale: string;
      iteration: number; iterationsRemaining: number; note: string }
  | { kind: "message"; text: string; preset: Preset | null; iteration: number }
  | { kind: "done";    text: string; preset: Preset; presetId: string; distance: number | null }
  | { kind: "error";   message: string; retryable: boolean };
```

**Every endpoint returns a `Step`.** That unification is what keeps this small — and it means a chat turn ("brighter") flows through the *identical* client code path as the initial refinement loop, because Claude answering "brighter" by calling `propose_preset` just yields another `{kind:"render"}`.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/session` | — | `{ sessionId: string }` |
| `POST` | `/api/session/:id/target` | `{ features: FeatureVector, info: TargetInfo }` | `Step` |
| `POST` | `/api/session/:id/analysis` | `{ presetId, features: FeatureVector, diff: FeatureDiff }` | `Step` |
| `POST` | `/api/session/:id/render-error` | `{ presetId, message: string }` | `Step` |
| `POST` | `/api/session/:id/chat` | `{ message: string }` | `Step` |
| `GET` | `/api/session/:id` | — | `SessionSnapshot` |

### The client is ~10 lines

```ts
// src/client/main.ts
async function drain(step: Step) {
  while (step.kind === "render") {
    ui.showAttempt(step);
    try {
      const buf   = await renderPreset(step.preset);        // OfflineAudioContext
      const got   = analyze(buf);                            // same STFT features as target
      const diff  = compareFeatures(targetFeatures, got);
      step = await api.submitAnalysis(sessionId, step.presetId, got, diff);
    } catch (e) {
      // a bad preset must not wedge the loop — tell the agent, let it retry
      step = await api.submitRenderError(sessionId, step.presetId, String(e));
    }
  }
  ui.showFinal(step);
}
```

The `try/catch → submitRenderError` path is **mandatory, not optional polish**. Structured-output JSON Schema cannot express numeric ranges (see §6), so Claude *can* hand you `ratio: 240` or `env.a: -1`. Without the catch, one bad preset stalls the session forever. With it, the DO appends a `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and Claude self-corrects — which is arguably a better demo than silent clamping.

### The DO driver

```ts
private async runClaude(force: boolean): Promise<Step> {
  this.meta.status = "thinking"; this.persist();
  try {
    const res = await this.anthropic.messages.create({
      model: "claude-sonnet-5",
      max_tokens: 2048,
      thinking: { type: "adaptive" },
      output_config: { effort: "low" },
      system: SYSTEM_BLOCKS,              // cache_control on last block
      tools: TOOLS,
      tool_choice: force
        ? { type: "any",  disable_parallel_tool_use: true }   // refinement loop: must act
        : { type: "auto", disable_parallel_tool_use: true },  // chat: may just answer
      messages: this.loadMessages(),
    });

    this.appendMessage({ role: "assistant", content: res.content });

    const text = res.content.filter(b => b.type === "text").map(b => b.text).join("");
    const tool = res.content.find(b => b.type === "tool_use");

    if (!tool) { this.meta.status = "idle"; this.persist(); return { kind: "message", text, ... }; }

    if (tool.name === "propose_preset") {
      const presetId = crypto.randomUUID();
      this.meta.pendingToolUseId = tool.id;       // ← the paused state, persisted
      this.meta.pendingPresetId  = presetId;
      this.meta.status = "awaiting_render";
      this.meta.history.push({ presetId, preset: tool.input.preset, rationale: tool.input.rationale,
                               features: null, distance: null });
      this.persist();
      return { kind: "render", presetId, preset: tool.input.preset,
               rationale: tool.input.rationale, note: text,
               iteration: this.meta.iteration,
               iterationsRemaining: this.meta.maxIterations - this.meta.iteration };
    }

    if (tool.name === "finalize") {
      this.appendMessage({ role: "user", content: [
        { type: "tool_result", tool_use_id: tool.id, content: "Finalized." }] });
      this.meta.status = "done"; this.meta.pendingToolUseId = null; this.persist();
      return { kind: "done", text, preset: tool.input.preset, ... };
    }
  } catch (e) {
    // CRITICAL: never leave status stuck on "thinking" — that wedges the session
    this.meta.status = this.meta.pendingToolUseId ? "awaiting_render" : "idle";
    this.persist();
    return { kind: "error", message: String(e), retryable: true };
  }
}
```

And the resume:

```ts
async submitAnalysis(presetId: string, features: FeatureVector, diff: FeatureDiff): Promise<Step> {
  if (this.meta.status !== "awaiting_render") throw new Error("not awaiting a render");
  if (presetId !== this.meta.pendingPresetId) throw new Error("stale render");   // idempotency guard

  this.meta.iteration += 1;
  const remaining = this.meta.maxIterations - this.meta.iteration;

  this.appendMessage({ role: "user", content: [{
    type: "tool_result",
    tool_use_id: this.meta.pendingToolUseId!,        // ← the id we parked one HTTP request ago
    content: JSON.stringify({
      distance: diff.distance,
      per_feature: diff.perFeature,   // { centroidHz: {target, got, delta_pct}, ... }
      iteration: this.meta.iteration,
      iterations_remaining: remaining,
      best_distance_so_far: this.bestDistance(),
      note: remaining === 0
        ? "Budget exhausted. Call finalize now with the best preset you have found."
        : "Propose your next preset, or call finalize if this is close enough."
    }),
  }]});
  this.meta.pendingToolUseId = null;
  this.recordResult(presetId, features, diff.distance);
  this.persist();

  return this.runClaude(/* force */ true);
}
```

The `presetId` equality check is the whole idempotency story: a double-click, a retry, or a reload mid-render can't desync the conversation — the second POST just 409s.

### WebSockets vs plain HTTP — recommendation: **plain HTTP**

Take HTTP request/response. Justification for a 2-hour box:

**For HTTP:**
- The protocol is *inherently* request/response. There is exactly one outstanding operation at any moment, and nothing ever happens server-side without the client asking. There is no server-push requirement — the primary motivation for WebSockets simply isn't present.
- With DO RPC, the entire transport is `const step = await env.SESSION.getByName(id).submitAnalysis(...)`. That's the whole thing.
- Reload/reconnect is free: `GET /api/session/:id` returns the snapshot and the client resumes from `status`.

**Against WebSockets here:**
- The hibernation API needs `acceptWebSocket`, `webSocketMessage`, `webSocketClose`, plus your own message framing, request/response correlation ids, and client-side reconnect. Realistically 40–50 minutes — a quarter of the budget — and it's the layer most likely to differ between `vite dev` and production.
- It buys you exactly one thing you'd notice: token streaming in chat. A spinner is acceptable in a prototype.
- Non-streaming also gives you a single code path for extracting `tool_use` (no `content_block_delta` accumulation, no partial-JSON assembly).

**The latency check that makes this safe:** Cloudflare's HTTP request ceiling is ~100s. A non-streaming `claude-sonnet-5` call at `effort: "low"` with `max_tokens: 2048` lands in roughly 3–10s. Comfortable margin. If you later find chat feels sluggish, add SSE (`ReadableStream` from the Worker) before reaching for WebSockets — SSE is one-directional and half the work.

## 6. Claude API usage

### Model: `claude-sonnet-5`

You asked for a fast model for the refine iterations, and this is the right pick over Haiku. Sonnet 5 delivers near-Opus quality on agentic/tool-use work at $3/$15 per MTok (**$2/$10 introductory through 2026-08-31 — you're inside that window today**), with a 1M context window. Haiku 4.5 would be cheaper but the sound-design reasoning — mapping a spectral-centroid delta to a modulation-index change — is exactly the kind of causal inference where the tier gap shows.

Request parameters:

```ts
{
  model: "claude-sonnet-5",
  max_tokens: 2048,                          // preset JSON + one rationale sentence is small
  thinking: { type: "adaptive" },            // NOT "disabled" — see below
  output_config: { effort: "low" },          // the speed lever
  tool_choice: { type: "any", disable_parallel_tool_use: true },
}
```

Three non-obvious points:

1. **Do not set `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`.** On Sonnet 5, thinking-off makes the model *less* likely to reach for tools — which is precisely the behavior your loop depends on. Use `thinking: {type:"adaptive"}` and control speed with `effort: "low"` instead. On Sonnet 5 adaptive is the default anyway (omitting `thinking` runs adaptive — a change from Sonnet 4.6).
2. **`disable_parallel_tool_use: true` is load-bearing.** Without it, Claude may emit two `propose_preset` blocks in one turn, and you can only render one at a time. You'd have to either render both or return a malformed result set. Force one.
3. **`tool_choice: {type:"any"}` during refinement, `{type:"auto"}` during chat.** In the loop you want action, not commentary. In chat, "what does the feedback parameter do?" should get a text answer, not a forced preset.

### Tool definitions

```ts
const OPERATOR_SCHEMA = {
  type: "object",
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ["ratio", "fixedHz", "level", "detune", "env", "velSens"],
  properties: {
    ratio:   { type: "number", description: "Frequency multiple of the played note. 0.25–16. Integer ratios (1,2,3,4) give harmonic tones; non-integer (1.41, 3.14, 7.13) give bell/metallic inharmonicity." },
    fixedHz: { type: "number", description: "If greater than 0, this operator runs at a fixed absolute frequency in Hz and ignores `ratio`. Use 0 for normal ratio mode. Useful for fixed formants or noise-like beds." },
    level:   { type: "number", description: "0–1. For a carrier this is output amplitude; for a modulator this is the modulation index — the single most powerful control over brightness/harmonic count." },
    detune:  { type: "number", description: "Cents, -100 to 100. Small values thicken; large values on a modulator add inharmonicity and beating." },
    env: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["a", "d", "s", "r"],
      properties: {
        a: { type: "number", description: "Attack seconds, 0.001–2." },
        d: { type: "number", description: "Decay seconds, 0.001–4." },
        s: { type: "number", description: "Sustain level 0–1." },
        r: { type: "number", description: "Release seconds, 0.001–4." }
      }
    },
    velSens: { type: "number", description: "0–1 velocity sensitivity." }
  }
} as const;

const PRESET_SCHEMA = {
  type: "object",
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ["algorithm", "feedback", "ops", "lfo", "master"],
  properties: {
    algorithm: { type: "integer", description: "0–7. See the algorithm table in the system prompt." },
    feedback:  { type: "number", description: "0–1. Self-modulation of the feedback operator. Above ~0.7 it approaches noise — the main lever for gritty/noisy timbres." },
    ops: { type: "array", items: OPERATOR_SCHEMA, description: "Exactly 4 operators, index 0–3. Which are carriers vs modulators is determined by `algorithm`." },
    lfo: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["rate", "depth", "target"],
      properties: {
        rate:   { type: "number", description: "Hz, 0.05–20." },
        depth:  { type: "number", description: "0–1." },
        target: { type: "string", enum: ["pitch", "amp", "mod"] }
      }
    },
    master: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["gain", "pitchEnv"],
      properties: {
        gain:     { type: "number", description: "0–1 output gain." },
        pitchEnv: { type: "number", description: "-1 to 1. Short pitch sweep at note start; positive values give percussive attack 'blip'." }
      }
    }
  }
} as const;

export const TOOLS = [
  {
    name: "propose_preset",
    strict: true,
    description:
      "Propose a 4-operator FM preset to test. The browser will render this preset offline with " +
      "OfflineAudioContext, compute the exact same STFT feature vector that was computed for the " +
      "target sample, and return you a per-feature diff plus a scalar distance as the tool result. " +
      "This is your measurement instrument — use it to test one hypothesis at a time. " +
      "You must call this at least once before calling finalize.",
    input_schema: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["preset", "rationale"],
      properties: {
        preset: PRESET_SCHEMA,
        rationale: { type: "string", description: "One sentence: what you changed relative to the previous attempt, and which specific feature you expect it to move and in which direction." }
      }
    }
  },
  {
    name: "finalize",
    strict: true,
    description:
      "Lock in your best preset and stop iterating. Call this when the distance has stopped " +
      "improving, the match is subjectively good enough, or `iterations_remaining` has reached 0.",
    input_schema: {
      type: "object", additionalProperties: false,
      required: ["preset", "rationale"],
      properties: {
        preset: PRESET_SCHEMA,
        rationale: { type: "string", description: "Two or three sentences for the user: what kind of sound this is, which FM techniques produce it, and where it still differs from the target." }
      }
    }
  }
];
```

**Two schema gotchas that will bite you if unflagged:**

1. **`strict: true` requires every property in `required` and `additionalProperties: false` everywhere.** That kills an optional `fixedHz?`. Two fixes: the `0` sentinel used above (simplest — one line in the engine: `const f = op.fixedHz > 0 ? op.fixedHz : noteHz * op.ratio`), or `{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"},{"type":"null"}]}` with `fixedHz` still listed in `required`. **Take the sentinel.** Make sure the DSP agent knows about it — it belongs in `src/shared/preset.ts` as a documented comment.
2. **Structured outputs do not support `minimum` / `maximum` / `minLength` / array-length constraints.** You cannot enforce "ratio between 0.25 and 16" or "exactly 4 operators" in the schema. Ranges live in the `description` strings (as above), and enforcement is the client-side `try/catch → submitRenderError` path plus, if there's time, a `sanitizePreset()` clamp.

### System prompt sketch

Five sections. The critical structural rule: **section 2 is generated from `src/shared/algorithms.ts`, never hand-written**, so the prompt cannot drift from the engine.

```ts
// src/worker/agent.ts
export const SYSTEM_BLOCKS = [
  { type: "text", text: `
You are a sound designer operating a 4-operator FM synthesizer through a closed measurement loop.

## How this loop works
The user uploaded an audio sample. The browser computed an STFT-derived feature vector from it —
that is your TARGET. You propose a preset with the propose_preset tool. The browser renders it
offline, computes the identical feature vector, and returns you a per-feature diff. You then
propose a refinement. You have a small, fixed iteration budget; every tool result tells you how
many iterations remain.

You are matching a *feature vector*, not a waveform. Your goal is to reduce the reported distance
while producing a preset that is musically sensible. Change one or two things per iteration and
say what you expect them to do — a controlled experiment beats a shotgun.

## The 4-operator FM engine
Four operators. Each is a sine oscillator with its own frequency ratio (or fixed Hz), output
level, detune, and ADSR envelope. Whether an operator is a CARRIER (its output is heard) or a
MODULATOR (its output modulates another operator's phase) is determined entirely by the algorithm.

Core causal facts, in rough order of leverage:
- A modulator's \`level\` is the modulation index. Raising it adds sidebands: more partials,
  brighter, denser. This is your primary brightness control.
- A modulator's \`ratio\` sets sideband SPACING. Integer ratios (1,2,3,4) produce harmonic,
  pitched, instrument-like spectra. Non-integer ratios (1.41, 2.73, 3.14, 7.13) produce
  inharmonic, bell-like, metallic, or clangorous spectra.
- Ratio 1:1 gives a sawtooth-ish full harmonic series. 2:1 emphasises even harmonics
  (clarinet/hollow character comes from odd-only, which you get around 3:1 with low index).
- \`feedback\` is an operator modulating itself. Low values add harmonics smoothly;
  above roughly 0.7 the spectrum breaks into noise. This is how you get grit, breath, and
  noise beds without a noise generator.
- The MODULATOR's envelope shapes TIMBRE OVER TIME; the CARRIER's envelope shapes LOUDNESS
  over time. A modulator decay shorter than the carrier decay gives the classic
  "bright attack that mellows out" — the signature of struck and plucked sounds.
- \`master.pitchEnv\` is a fast pitch sweep at note start. Positive values give a percussive
  click/blip attack (drums, mallets).
- \`detune\` on modulators adds beating and mild inharmonicity; on carriers it thickens.

## The 8 algorithms
${renderAlgorithmTable(ALGORITHMS)}   // generated from src/shared/algorithms.ts

## How to read the feature diff
Each tool result gives you \`distance\` (lower is better) and \`per_feature\`, where each entry is
{ target, got, delta_pct }. Positive delta_pct means your render measured HIGHER than the target.

- centroidHz        Spectral brightness. Too low -> raise modulator level, or raise modulator
                    ratio. Too high -> lower modulator level first; it is the blunter instrument.
- centroidSlope     How brightness changes from attack to decay. Target more negative than yours
                    -> shorten the modulator's env.d relative to the carrier's.
- flatness          0 = pure tone, 1 = noise. Too low -> raise feedback, or move a modulator to a
                    non-integer ratio. Too high -> reduce feedback and return to integer ratios.
- inharmonicity     Directly controlled by non-integer modulator ratios and heavy detune.
- oddEvenRatio      Ratio choice. ~3:1 with modest index leans odd (hollow, clarinet-like);
                    ~2:1 gives a fuller odd+even spectrum.
- attackMs          Carrier env.a. For attack *bite* specifically, shorten the modulator's env.a
                    while keeping its level high.
- decayMs / sustainLevel / releaseMs   Carrier env.d / env.s / env.r.
- bands[]           Coarse log-spaced spectral shape. A target with energy concentrated in a
                    single band region suggests a simpler algorithm with fewer parallel carriers;
                    energy spread across many bands suggests parallel carriers or higher feedback.

## Working rules
1. First proposal: read the target vector holistically and pick a plausible ARCHETYPE
   (struck metal / plucked string / brass / electric piano / bass / pad / noisy percussion),
   then instantiate it. Do not start from a default sine.
2. Each later proposal: pick the ONE or TWO features with the largest weighted error and address
   them specifically. State the expectation in \`rationale\`.
3. If a change moved a feature the wrong way, reverse it rather than compounding it.
4. When \`iterations_remaining\` reaches 0, call finalize with the best preset you have seen,
   not necessarily the most recent one.
5. Later, the user will chat with you to tweak the sound in plain language ("brighter",
   "more attack bite", "less metallic"). Translate those to specific parameter moves using the
   causal facts above, propose the preset, and let the measurement confirm it.
`.trim(),
    cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }   // system + tools are stable; cache them
  }
];
```

`cache_control` on the last system block caches tools + system together (render order is tools → system → messages). Sonnet 5's minimum cacheable prefix is 1024 tokens; the block above plus the tool schemas clears that comfortably. Every turn after the first in a session reads it at ~0.1×. Verify with `response.usage.cache_read_input_tokens` — if it's 0 across turns, something in the prefix is varying.

| **7** | 1:35–1:50 | Chat box → `/chat` → same `drain()`. Distance-per-iteration list, play buttons for target and current preset. Minimal CSS. | Demoable |
